evidence.detail: The exact base-to-target diff changes nine allowed implementation/test/governance paths. git diff --check completed successfully.
The Graph-only unit module completed: 11 tests passed with exit 0.

The full suite ran 46 tests but exited 1 because all 10 server integration tests were unable to bind a loopback socket in the review sandbox; 36 tests completed without reported failures before those environment errors.
Compilation could not run because the read-only checkout prevented creation of __pycache__.
Governance validation could not complete because the sandbox offered no writable temporary directory.

Static inspection confirms repair-round protections: HTTPS and exact graph.microsoft.com hostname validation, rejection of embedded credentials, disabled automatic redirects, cycle detection, and a 200-page bound that raises rather than returning partial data.

evidence: Expected: the normalized contract must accurately represent session controls consumed by ISSUE-0004.
Observed: normalize_policy adds every recognized session-control object to sessionControls solely when its value is a dict; it neither checks isEnabled nor preserves control settings.

A Graph object such as persistentBrowser: {"isEnabled": false, "mode": "never"} is therefore normalized identically to an enabled control, while signInFrequency value/type and other rule-relevant settings are discarded.
The test fixture omits isEnabled and asserts only the control name, so this semantic loss is encoded as expected behavior.
findings.remediation: Define and implement a session-control shape that preserves each control's enabled state and analyzer-relevant settings, or explicitly include only controls whose isEnabled value is true. Update the durable contract and normalization tests with enabled and disabled examples.
findings.title: Session-control normalization treats disabled controls as enabled and discards their settings
findings.verification: Normalize fixtures containing enabled and disabled persistentBrowser/signInFrequency controls and verify the result distinguishes them and preserves every field required by ISSUE-0004; rerun the full suite.

evidence: Expected: mocked tests demonstrate that /api/policies returns normalized policies and maps a Graph 403 to a clear structured consent response, as required by acceptance criteria 1, 3, and 4.

Observed: the only added server test exercises the unauthenticated 401 path. Success, paging-through-the-endpoint, 403 mapping, and generic Graph-error mapping are tested only at GraphClient level or not at all.

The handoff nevertheless marks the endpoint criteria met by citing test_single_page_normalizes and test_403_is_consent_required, both of which call GraphClient directly and cannot detect routing, status, or response-envelope regressions in server._policies.
findings.remediation: Add mocked endpoint tests with an in-memory token and injected Graph client for successful normalized output and 403 consent_required behavior; also cover the structured 502 path. Avoid real network access.
findings.title: Acceptance-critical /api/policies success and consent paths lack endpoint tests
findings.verification: Run the endpoint tests and confirm HTTP 200 returns {policies, count}, Graph consent_required returns HTTP 403 with the actionable message, and other Graph errors return the documented structured response.

evidence: Expected: repository records durably identify the exact repair candidate under review, as required by AGENTS.md and the prior F-004 remediation.
Observed: the issue record's Candidate SHA still names only the round-0 candidate 2495c32df08ee11a563122bde4a5fca6fe93fae1 and says repair candidates rebind at review time.

The repair handoff says Candidate SHA is "this commit" and CURRENT.md says branch HEAD; none records exact SHA 25621bb389b184f8eb23b89821e530f769595647. The candidate identity therefore depends on launcher context rather than repository files alone.
findings.remediation: Bind repair round 1 explicitly to 25621bb389b184f8eb23b89821e530f769595647 in the issue round table and candidate metadata, handoff, and status record. A metadata-only follow-up must clearly state that the reviewed product SHA remains 25621bb389b184f8eb23b89821e530f769595647.
findings.title: Durable records still do not name the exact repair candidate
findings.verification: Inspect the issue, handoff, and CURRENT.md and run the governance validator; all should agree on the exact base, repair-round product SHA, review round, and next action.

evidence: Expected: repair F-003 verification explicitly required both a repeated next link and a sequence exceeding MAX_PAGES to raise rather than return partial results.
Observed: test_paging_cycle_detected covers only the repeated-link case. No test exercises the MAX_PAGES boundary or an over-limit sequence.
The bound appears correct by inspection, but the claimed repair is not fully verified and future off-by-one changes could restore partial-success behavior.
findings.remediation: Add a generated mocked sequence that reaches the page limit with another next link pending and assert GraphError plus no successful partial return. Also verify the precise permitted-page boundary.
findings.title: The repaired paging limit has no boundary test
findings.verification: Run tests for MAX_PAGES pages and MAX_PAGES plus a pending next link, confirming the documented boundary and structured error behavior.

limitations: The mandatory full test suite did not pass in this read-only review sandbox because loopback socket binding is prohibited; all 10 server integration tests errored before their assertions.
Compilation could not be independently verified because py_compile requires filesystem writes for bytecode output.
Governance validation could not complete because its launcher smoke tests require a writable temporary directory.

The committed handoff reports successful compile, 46-test, and governance runs, but raw immutable command output bound to target SHA 25621bb389b184f8eb23b89821e530f769595647 is not committed; those statements remain author claims.
The protected live Graph fetch was not attempted, so real tenant consent behavior, response compatibility, and live paging remain unverified by design.
Redirect refusal was verified statically but lacks a transport-level test using the default urllib opener.
No test exercises malformed successful Graph payload shapes; nested non-object values can currently raise AttributeError or TypeError rather than GraphError.
review.summary: BLOCKED. Base and target identity match, the working tree is clean, Graph unit tests pass, and the prior token-exfiltration and partial-paging repairs are materially improved. However, mandatory independent full-suite, compile, and governance evidence could not complete in the read-only sandbox. Static review also found inaccurate session-control normalization, missing endpoint-level acceptance tests, incomplete exact-SHA metadata, and an untested page-limit boundary.
